additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs lasting at least one month, with functioning often relatively preserved outside the area affected by the belief. It typically presents in midlife or later but can occur in younger adults, and it is distinguished from schizophrenia by the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or broad deterioration in functioning.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient.stressor: During a long-planned kitchen and garden remodeling project, Lissette’s usually orderly home life was disrupted by workers, delays, misplaced materials, and repeated budget adjustments that interfered with cooking for community events and hosting family gatherings. Over the next 1 year and 9 months, her initial frustration hardened into fixed beliefs about the people involved in the remodeling and the neighborhood changes around her, and reassurance from her husband, receipts, and contractor explanations did little to shift her interpretation. She continued attending book club, church-related gatherings, and heritage festival meetings, but the belief increasingly shaped whom she trusted and how she handled ordinary household decisions. She came to psychiatric care after her primary care physician, whom she had known for years, suggested a consultation when repeated visits about the same home-related concerns did not resolve despite practical evidence being reviewed with her.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: Outside of dealing with the remodel, I still keep up with my church gatherings, book club, household routines, and family plans the way I usually do.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve stopped trusting certain neighbors and workers, and my husband has had to take over more of the remodeling decisions because I keep questioning what people are really doing.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 1 year and 9 months, since the kitchen and garden remodeling started disrupting the house.
